disposition: piperine held constant in a menstrual sleep trial
assessment: Both arms received piperine, so the comparison cannot isolate piperine or ground pepper. Participants had dysmenorrhea and premenstrual symptoms.

disposition: piperine held constant in a menstrual pain trial
assessment: Piperine was in both capsule arms. The baseline VAS and the trial's menstrual endpoints do not test pain after black pepper in Parkinson disease.
The trial contrasts curcumin with lactose while holding piperine constant. The pain observations concern menstrual symptoms and a different population.

disposition: curcumin and Epworth sleepiness outside Parkinson
assessment: The randomized Epworth comparison was inconclusive. The study tested curcumin capsules with piperine in people with primary dysmenorrhea.

disposition: green oat extract and smoking-related sleep
assessment: Actigraphic wake after sleep onset favored green oat extract at eight weeks. The trial did not test rolled oats or measure clinical Parkinson insomnia.

disposition: sage cross-reference in a savory enzyme assay
assessment: The discussion mentions sage in earlier cholinesterase assays. The primary tests did not administer sage or assess pain.

disposition: traditional savory pain use in background

disposition: constituent language in savory enzyme and chemistry paper

The study used sage extract, isolated rosmarinic and caffeic acids, and an antidepressant drug comparator. It measured pain after nerve injury and gives no rosemary exposure or clinical depression result.

disposition: sage extract in a neuropathic pain model
assessment: Oral sage extract improved several pain-related behaviors in mice after sciatic constriction. The exposure was ethanolic extract and the model was peripheral injury.

disposition: turmeric and pepper extracts in postinfectious smell loss
assessment: Two uncontrolled cases reported improved smell after taking combination extracts following COVID-19. Both contained black pepper extract and one contained Boswellia. The cases do not isolate either ingredient or measure Parkinson hyposmia.
The turmeric-containing granule reduced insomnia and nightmare ratings and altered nocturnal activity. No dedicated daytime sleepiness scale was reported and the design did not isolate turmeric.
